superior.simpleDefinition: Higher in rank, status, quality, or excellence than others.
superior.example: Handcrafted leather shoes are clearly superior in durability to synthetic footwear.

supplant.simpleDefinition: To supersede and replace someone or something, often through innovation or force.
supplant.example: Modern smartphones have largely supplanted portable music players and calculators.

surreal.simpleDefinition: Having a bizarre, dreamlike, or unreal quality; strange.
surreal.example: Walking through the completely empty airport at midnight felt quiet and surreal.

susceptible.simpleDefinition: Likely or liable to be influenced, harmed, or affected by a particular thing.
susceptible.example: Young seedlings are especially susceptible to frost damage during chilly spring nights.

suspect.simpleDefinition: A person thought to be guilty of a crime or offense under investigation.
suspect.example: Police questioned the suspect about his whereabouts at the time of the burglary.

swindle.simpleDefinition: To cheat or defraud someone out of money or possessions using deception.
swindle.example: The con artist attempted to swindle unsuspecting tourists with counterfeit jewelry.

swollen.simpleDefinition: Enlarged or puffed up, typically from injury, inflammation, or fluid buildup.
swollen.example: Her ankle became painfully swollen after she twisted it during the soccer match.

sycophancy.simpleDefinition: Obsequious, flattering behavior toward someone important in order to gain advantage.
sycophancy.example: The vain executive was surrounded by sycophancy that concealed real corporate problems.

synopsis.simpleDefinition: A brief summary or general overview of a book, play, or other work.
synopsis.example: The author submitted a two-page synopsis along with the first chapter of her manuscript.

taciturn.simpleDefinition: Reserved, uncommunicative, and saying very little by nature.
taciturn.example: The taciturn old farmer rarely spoke more than a few words at breakfast.

tantamount.simpleDefinition: Equivalent in seriousness, effect, or value to something.
tantamount.example: Refusing to testify was considered tantamount to an admission of guilt.

taunting.simpleDefinition: Provoking or challenging someone with insulting or contemptuous remarks.
taunting.example: The bully was caught taunting younger students on the playground.

telepathy.simpleDefinition: The supposed communication of thoughts or ideas by means other than the known senses.
telepathy.example: Science fiction novels often portray alien species communicating through silent telepathy.

teller.simpleDefinition: A bank employee whose job is to pay out and take in money at the counter.
teller.example: The bank teller counted the cash carefully before handing over the receipt.

tenacity.simpleDefinition: The quality or fact of being determined, persistent, and holding firmly to a goal.
tenacity.example: Her tenacity helped her overcome severe illness and graduate with highest honors.

tenant.simpleDefinition: A person who occupies land or property rented from a landlord.
tenant.example: The tenant paid his monthly rent on the first day of every month.

tender.simpleDefinition: Showing gentleness, kindness, and affection, or easy to cut and chew.
tender.example: The nurse dressed the child's wound with tender care and soothing words.

tentative.simpleDefinition: Not certain or fixed; provisional, or done with hesitation.
tentative.example: We made a tentative agreement to meet for coffee next Thursday afternoon.

tenterhooks.simpleDefinition: In a state of painful suspense, acute tension, or anxiety.
tenterhooks.example: The candidate was on tenterhooks all evening waiting for election results.

tenure.simpleDefinition: The conditions under which land or buildings are held, or permanent employment status.
tenure.example: After seven years of successful research, the university granted him academic tenure.

tepid.simpleDefinition: Only slightly warm; lukewarm, or showing little enthusiasm.
tepid.example: The new comedy film received only tepid applause from the opening night audience.

thankless.simpleDefinition: Difficult or unpleasant and unlikely to result in thanks or reward.
thankless.example: Cleaning up after the messy outdoor festival was a difficult and thankless job.

theist.simpleDefinition: A person who believes in the existence of a God or gods.
theist.example: As a devoted theist, he found meaning and comfort in daily prayer.

theologist.simpleDefinition: A person who studies religion, religious beliefs, and the divine.
theologist.example: The theologist gave a fascinating lecture comparing ancient scriptures.

thorough.simpleDefinition: Complete with regard to every detail; meticulously rigorous.
thorough.example: The mechanics performed a thorough inspection of the aircraft before takeoff.

thread.simpleDefinition: A long, thin strand of cotton, nylon, or other fibers used in sewing.
thread.example: She carefully guided the black thread through the eye of the sewing needle.

thrifty.simpleDefinition: Using money and other resources carefully and not wastefully; economical.
thrifty.example: Her thrifty shopping habits enabled the family to save money for a home.

tiny in size.simpleDefinition: Extremely small in physical dimensions or magnitude.
tiny in size.example: The electronic microchip was tiny in size but packed immense computing power.

tipped.simpleDefinition: Gave a sum of money to someone for service, or overturned or tilted.
tipped.example: He tipped the polite restaurant waiter generously for exceptional service.

tirade.simpleDefinition: A long, angry speech of criticism, reprimand, or accusation.
tirade.example: The coach launched into an angry tirade after the team made sloppy defensive errors.

titanic.simpleDefinition: Of exceptional strength, size, power, or influence; colossal.
titanic.example: The two rival football clubs fought a titanic struggle for the championship cup.

to blow hot and cold.simpleDefinition: To alternate between enthusiasm and indifference; be vacillating.
to blow hot and cold.example: The client keeps blowing hot and cold on whether to sign the software contract.

to do away with.simpleDefinition: To abolish, discard, eliminate, or stop using something.
to do away with.example: The city voted to do away with outdated paper parking tickets.

to drive off.simpleDefinition: To force someone or something to leave or retreat, or depart in a car.
to drive off.example: The brave guard dog barked loudly to drive off the wild coyotes.

tomb.simpleDefinition: A large vault or chamber, typically underground, for burying the dead.
tomb.example: Archaeologists carefully uncovered the ancient pharaoh's gilded tomb in Egypt.

toot your own horn.simpleDefinition: To talk boastfully about one's own achievements or skills.
toot your own horn.example: I hate to toot my own horn, but I was the one who solved that complex problem.

toppling.simpleDefinition: Overbalancing or causing something to fall over; overthrowing.
toppling.example: Strong coastal winds were responsible for toppling the old oak tree.

torpor.simpleDefinition: A state of physical or mental inactivity, lethargy, or sluggishness.
torpor.example: The oppressive tropical heat plunged the entire village into an afternoon torpor.

tough.simpleDefinition: Strong enough to withstand adverse conditions or rough handling; difficult.
tough.example: Hiking through the dense snowy mountains was a tough physical test.

towered high.simpleDefinition: Rose or stood to an impressive, extraordinary height.
towered high.example: The snow-capped peaks of the Himalayas towered high above the clouds.

tract.simpleDefinition: An area of land, or a major passage in the body, or a short written pamphlet.
tract.example: The nature reserve covers a vast tract of pristine pine forest.

traduce.simpleDefinition: To speak badly of or tell lies about someone so as to damage their reputation.
traduce.example: The rival candidate attempted to traduce her good character through slanderous ads.

traitor.simpleDefinition: A person who betrays a friend, country, or principle.
traitor.example: The military spy was court-martialed and condemned as a traitor to his nation.

transient.simpleDefinition: Lasting only for a short time; impermanent and fleeting.
transient.example: Youth and spring blossoms are beautiful but transient stages of life.

transmission.simpleDefinition: The action of broadcasting or sending something, or the passing on of disease.
transmission.example: Wearing masks helped prevent the airborne transmission of the seasonal flu.

transmit.simpleDefinition: To cause something to pass on from one place or person to another.
transmit.example: Radio antennas transmit communication signals across thousands of miles.

trapped.simpleDefinition: Caught in a trap or difficult situation from which escape is hard.
trapped.example: Firefighters used heavy ladders to rescue the families trapped on the third floor.

treatise.simpleDefinition: A written work dealing formally and systematically with a subject.
treatise.example: The philosopher published a celebrated treatise on human ethics and political liberty.

trespass.simpleDefinition: To enter someone's land or property without permission.
trespass.example: Signs were posted along the boundary warning hikers not to trespass on private grounds.

trial.simpleDefinition: A formal examination of evidence in court, or a test of performance or hardship.
trial.example: The high-profile murder trial lasted four weeks before the jury reached a verdict.

trick.simpleDefinition: A cunning or skillful act or scheme intended to deceive or entertain.
trick.example: The clever magician performed an astonishing card trick right in front of our eyes.

trickery.simpleDefinition: The practice of deception, fraud, or cunning tricks.
trickery.example: The fraudster used clever trickery to persuade the victim to hand over her savings.

triumph.simpleDefinition: A great victory, achievement, or success.
triumph.example: Winning the championship tournament was the crowning triumph of her tennis career.

troops.simpleDefinition: Soldiers or armed forces grouped for military service.
troops.example: Peacekeeping troops were deployed to maintain calm in the border region.

truant.simpleDefinition: A student who stays away from school without leave or explanation.
truant.example: The truant officer returned the wandering boys to school before noon.

trustworthy.simpleDefinition: Able to be relied on as honest, dependable, or truthful.
trustworthy.example: He has proven himself to be a completely trustworthy and diligent business partner.

turbid.simpleDefinition: Cloudy, opaque, or thick with suspended matter (of a liquid); or confused.
turbid.example: Heavy torrential rains turned the mountain river turbid and brown.

ulterior.simpleDefinition: Existing beyond what is obvious or admitted; intentionally concealed.
ulterior.example: She suspected that his unexpected generosity masked an ulterior selfish motive.

uncover.simpleDefinition: To remove a cover or covering, or discover previously hidden facts.
uncover.example: Investigative reporters worked for months to uncover the truth behind the financial fraud.

understatement.simpleDefinition: The presentation of something as being smaller, worse, or less important than it actually is.
understatement.example: Calling a category-five hurricane 'a bit of windy weather' is a massive understatement.

undertake.simpleDefinition: To commit oneself to and begin an enterprise or responsibility.
undertake.example: The engineers agreed to undertake the repair of the ancient railway bridge.

unearth.simpleDefinition: To dig up something from the ground, or discover information after searching.
unearth.example: Archaeologists managed to unearth golden artifacts buried for thousands of years.

unequivocal.simpleDefinition: Leaving no doubt; completely clear, explicit, and unambiguous.
unequivocal.example: The board gave its unequivocal support to the director's strategic vision.

unfathomable.simpleDefinition: Incapable of being fully explored, understood, or measured.
unfathomable.example: The motives behind the criminal's bizarre actions remained completely unfathomable.

unforeseen.example: Due to unforeseen weather delays, the afternoon flight was postponed until morning.

uniform.simpleDefinition: Remaining the same in all cases and at all times; consistent and unchanging.
uniform.example: The factory machines produced metal rods of strictly uniform thickness.

unimaginable.simpleDefinition: Difficult or impossible to imagine or comprehend; beyond belief.
unimaginable.example: The earthquake caused an almost unimaginable amount of structural damage to the city.

uninfluenced.simpleDefinition: Not affected, altered, or swayed by external pressure or bias.
uninfluenced.example: A judge must remain completely uninfluenced by media gossip or political pressure.

unintended.simpleDefinition: Not planned or meant to happen; accidental.
unintended.example: The new zoning regulation had the unintended consequence of raising house rents.

unruly.simpleDefinition: Disorderly, disruptive, and not amenable to discipline or control.
unruly.example: The teacher struggled to quiet down the noisy and unruly classroom.

unstable.simpleDefinition: Prone to change, fail, or sway; not firmly established or balanced.
unstable.example: Do not climb onto that wobbly stool because it is dangerously unstable.

untamed.simpleDefinition: Not domesticated, trained, or controlled; wild and natural.
untamed.example: The vast national park preserves miles of raw, untamed wilderness.

untenable.simpleDefinition: Not able to be maintained or defended against attack or objection.
untenable.example: After new facts emerged, the politician's original argument became completely untenable.

unwitting.simpleDefinition: Not done on purpose; unintentional, or not aware of the full facts.
unwitting.example: He became the unwitting accomplice in a scam when he forwarded a spoofed link.

upheld.simpleDefinition: Maintained, supported, or confirmed a decision, custom, or principle.
upheld.example: The supreme court upheld the lower court's ruling regarding environmental protection.

urban.simpleDefinition: In, relating to, or characteristic of a town or city.
urban.example: Many young professionals move to major urban centers in search of exciting career options.

urgency.simpleDefinition: Importance requiring swift, immediate action or attention.
urgency.example: The doctor stressed the urgency of taking the medication right away.

usurp.simpleDefinition: To take a position of power, throne, or authority illegally or by force.
usurp.example: The ruthless general led a military coup to usurp the presidency from the civilian leader.

utopia.simpleDefinition: An imagined community or society that possesses highly desirable or nearly perfect qualities.
utopia.example: The novelist depicted a future utopia where poverty, disease, and war had been eradicated.

vacillate.simpleDefinition: To alternate or waver between different opinions or actions; be indecisive.
vacillate.example: He continued to vacillate between studying law or pursuing a career in computer science.

vague.simpleDefinition: Thinking or communicating in an unfocused, imprecise, or indefinite way.
vague.example: His vague directions caused us to take two wrong turns on the way to the cabin.

valiant.simpleDefinition: Possessing or showing great courage, bravery, or determination.
valiant.example: The valiant firefighters rushed into the burning building to rescue the trapped family.

valley.simpleDefinition: A low area of land between hills or mountains, typically with a river flowing through it.
valley.example: The lush green valley was dotted with charming farmhouses and grazing cattle.

valorous.simpleDefinition: Showing great courage in the face of danger, especially in battle.
valorous.example: The knight received a royal medal for his valorous defense of the castle gates.

vehemently.simpleDefinition: In a forceful, passionate, or intense manner; with great feeling.
vehemently.example: The accused suspect vehemently denied having any involvement in the bank burglary.

velocity.simpleDefinition: The speed of something in a given direction.
velocity.example: The space rocket accelerated to orbital velocity within just a few minutes of launch.

vendor.simpleDefinition: A person or company offering something for sale, especially in the street.
vendor.example: A street vendor was roasting sweet corn over charcoal on the busy sidewalk.

venerate.simpleDefinition: To regard with great respect, admiration, or deep reverence.
venerate.example: Traditional cultures venerate elders for their lifelong wisdom and guidance.

venture.simpleDefinition: A risky or daring journey, or an undertaking involving financial uncertainty.
venture.example: Investing in the new tech startup was a daring venture that ultimately paid off.

venturesome.simpleDefinition: Willing to take risks or embark on difficult adventures; daring.
venturesome.example: The venturesome explorer traveled deep into uncharted Amazon rainforests.

versatility.simpleDefinition: Ability to adapt or be adapted to many different functions or activities.
versatility.example: Her versatility as an actress allowed her to play comedic and dramatic roles with equal skill.

vicious.simpleDefinition: Deliberately cruel, violent, or malicious; savage.
vicious.example: The hikers backed away slowly when they encountered a vicious guard dog.

vigor.simpleDefinition: Physical strength, good health, and energetic effort.
vigor.example: Despite his advanced age, the gardener worked with remarkable vigor and cheerfulness.

vigorous.simpleDefinition: Strong, healthy, and full of energy, or characterized by force and effort.
vigorous.example: Doctors recommend thirty minutes of vigorous physical exercise every day.

visible.simpleDefinition: Able to be seen or noticed; apparent and obvious.
visible.example: The snowy mountaintops were clearly visible from our hotel balcony.

visionary.simpleDefinition: A person with original ideas about what the future will or could be like.
visionary.example: The computer company was founded by a true visionary who foresaw mobile computing.

vital.simpleDefinition: Absolutely necessary or essential for life, success, or functioning.
vital.example: Clean drinking water and fresh food are vital for human health.

vocation.simpleDefinition: A strong feeling of suitability for a particular career, calling, or profession.
vocation.example: She felt a genuine calling and vocation to become a dedicated teacher.

vociferous.simpleDefinition: Expressing feelings or opinions loudly, passionately, and forcefully.
vociferous.example: There were vociferous protests outside city hall against the proposed budget cuts.

void.simpleDefinition: A completely empty space, or a feeling of deep emptiness or loss.
void.example: Her sudden retirement left an immense void in the research team.

voluptuous.simpleDefinition: Relating to or characterized by luxury, sensual pleasure, or curvy fullness.
voluptuous.example: The banquet featured voluptuous feasts served on golden platters.

vow.simpleDefinition: A solemn promise, pledge, or commitment to do something.
vow.example: They exchanged marriage vows in front of family and close friends.

voyage.simpleDefinition: A long journey involving travel by sea or in space.
voyage.example: The ancient explorers embarked on a perilous voyage across the Atlantic.

vulgarity.simpleDefinition: The quality of lacking taste, refinement, decency, or good manners.
vulgarity.example: The play was criticized by conservative reviewers for excessive vulgarity in its jokes.

wagon.simpleDefinition: A four-wheeled vehicle for carrying heavy loads, typically drawn by horses or a tractor.
wagon.example: The farmer loaded bushels of freshly picked apples into the wooden wagon.

waive.simpleDefinition: To refrain from insisting on or using a legal right, claim, or fee.
waive.example: The university agreed to waive the application fee for low-income applicants.

wallet.simpleDefinition: A pocket-sized flat folding case for holding money and credit cards.
wallet.example: He reached into his jacket pocket and pulled out his leather wallet.

wander.simpleDefinition: To walk or move in a leisurely, casual, or aimless way.
wander.example: They loved to wander through the quiet cobblestone alleys of the historic village.

warehouse.simpleDefinition: A large building where raw materials or manufactured goods are stored before sale.
warehouse.example: The distribution company stores pallets of electronics in a temperature-controlled warehouse.

warlock.simpleDefinition: A man who practices witchcraft or black magic; a sorcerer.
warlock.example: In fantasy tales, the dark warlock cast a spell over the sleeping kingdom.

wayward.simpleDefinition: Difficult to control or predict because of willful or perverse behavior.
wayward.example: The novel recounts the story of a wayward youth who reformed and found purpose.

wear out.simpleDefinition: To use something until it is no longer usable, or tire someone completely.
wear out.example: Daily running on concrete will quickly wear out the soles of your sneakers.

wholesale.simpleDefinition: The selling of goods in large quantities to retailers for resale, or extensive.
wholesale.example: The supermarket buys fresh dairy at wholesale prices directly from dairy farms.

wicked.simpleDefinition: Evil or morally wrong; deliberately intending to do harm.
wicked.example: In folklore, the wicked queen attempted to trick the innocent princess.

windy.simpleDefinition: Marked by or exposed to strong winds and gusts of air.
windy.example: A windy autumn day sent colorful leaves dancing across the lawn.

withhold.simpleDefinition: To refuse to give something that is due to or desired by another.
withhold.example: It is a crime to withhold critical evidence from investigators during a trial.

worsen.simpleDefinition: To make or become worse in quality, condition, or severity.
worsen.example: Air pollution tends to worsen during humid and windless winter evenings.

worship.simpleDefinition: To show reverence and adoration for a deity, or honor deeply.
worship.example: Devoted pilgrims travel across the country to worship at the ancient temple.

worth yours.simpleDefinition: Worth your time, effort, attention, or investment.
worth yours.example: Visiting the historical museum while in the capital is well worth your time.

worthy of.simpleDefinition: Deserving of respect, praise, support, or consideration.
worthy of.example: Her heroic volunteer efforts after the flood are truly worthy of public recognition.

writ.simpleDefinition: A formal written legal order issued by a court or judicial authority.
writ.example: The judge issued a writ of habeas corpus directing that the prisoner be brought to court.

yield.simpleDefinition: To produce or provide a crop or profit, or give way to arguments or pressure.
yield.example: Careful fertilization helped the farm yield its largest wheat harvest in a decade.

zest.simpleDefinition: Great enthusiasm, energy, and eagerness, or lively exciting flavor.
zest.example: She brought tremendous zest and creativity to every new educational project.
